text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The United States seeks progress and not a solution on the Cyprus issue before Cypriot presidential elections next year. Britain is disappointed by the absence of the Americans in attempts to find common ground on the dispute.

- The government spokesman steps in to defuse a row between Antenna television and the finance minister over critical remarks about the state of the economy made last week by politicans and broadcast on the channel.
- A British woman is held in a Paphos jail without a court order. She was arrested for allegedly working illegally.
- Former President George Vassiliou urges the government to go ahead with a unilateral suspension of flights by Greek war planes.
- Report on row that has broken out over claims that foreign minister's family firm breached terms of a building permit for the construction of a hotel in Paphos.
- A parliamentary committee recommends changes to the opening hours of shops.

- Athens is caught by surprise by the unexpected visit of Turkish chief of staff Ismail Hakki Karadayi at the Greek national day reception in Istanbul. "We are obliged to develop friendly relations," he says.
- Government doctors are considering another strike if their demands (adjustments to pension schemes) are not met.
-Finance minister insists on pay rises for senior state officials.
